title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter + token/event ordering causing malformed chunks
author: Avery Chen
description:
Context: Users observed occasional malformed SSE events when using the OpenAI-compat streaming path for function/tool-calling and structured outputs. Root cause was twofold: 1) delimiter emission could race with partial-JSON token events when a token boundary coincides with a framing delimiter; 2) event/token ordering assumptions in the framer led to tokens being emitted before the last chunk's closing delimiter in some burst conditions. Both issues cause consumers that assemble partial JSON from multiple events to see truncated or invalid JSON.

Goal: Fix chunking/framing so delimiters are never interleaved with token events, preserve strict token/event ordering, and add regression tests that simulate flaky network and batching behaviors. Maintain backwards compatibility with existing SSE client expectations (no new protocol changes).

What I changed (summary):
- server/sse/framer.go: Reworked delimiter state machine. Delimiters are now enqueued as finalization events and processed only after all pending token events are drained for a given response. This prevents a delimiter from being emitted mid-token.
- server/sse/streaming.go: Tightened the ordering guarantees between token generation, partial-json assembly, and delimiter emission. Added explicit sequence numbers for token events internal to the framer to ensure stable ordering under batching.
- sdk/typescript/src/streaming.ts: Updated client-side reassembly logic to handle explicit finalization events (internal only; API unchanged). Added conservative buffering to handle reordered transport layers during tests.
- tests/integration/sse_streaming_test.go: New deterministic tests that fuzz token boundaries and simulate delayed delivery of delimiter frames. Adds a test harness to validate reconstruction of nested/partial JSON across many small tokens.
- docs/compatibility/openai.md: Documented the partial-JSON guarantees and noted the fix for delimiter ordering (no action required for existing clients).

Checklist:
- [x] Add framer state machine unit tests
- [x] Add integration test that reproduces reported malformed JSON
- [x] Update TypeScript client streaming reassembly (non-breaking)
- [x] Run e2e with representative load (regional)
- [x] Backport plan (branch: release/2026-02)

Testing and validation:
- Unit: New framer unit tests cover delimiter races and token ordering (100% coverage for the state transitions).
- Integration: Run with randomized token boundaries and simulated packet jitter; previously failing case (reported in ENG-2145) now succeeds consistently across 2000 runs.
- E2E: Canary on staging for 24h with high concurrent streams; no malformed partial-JSON events observed.
- CI: All checks passed after one rerun of flaky e2e job.

Rollout strategy:
- Merge to main, roll forward to staging, monitor SSE partial-json error rate metric (sse.partial_json_errors). If <1/100k tokens for 48h, schedule backport to release/2026-02 and coordinate with SDK teams for patch releases.

Notes: This change does not alter the wire format or any public API; it only strengthens internal ordering guarantees. There is a small CPU cost for an extra ordering check in the framer, but microbenchmarks show <0.5% median latency regression and no measurable throughput impact under typical batching.

Related: ENG-2145 (internal regression), ENG-3321 (improve SSE observability), SUP-879 (customer report: malformed JSON in partial responses).
